newsitem.title: LEBANON: Iraqi diplomats to be freed on bail in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi diplomats to be freed on bail in Beirut.

text.p: A Lebanese investigative judge ordered on Monday the release on bail of three Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the 1994 murder of an Iraqi opposition leader in Beirut, judicial sources said.

They said Judge Saeed Mirza set bail at 50,000 Lebanese pounds ($32) for each of Mohamad Kazem, Ali Darwish and Hadi Hassan -- held without trial for over 30 months at Lebanon's biggest jail at Roumieh.
All three had been arrested immediately after the April 12, 1994 killing of Iraqi dissident Taleb as-Suheil.
The murder of Suheil, an opponent of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, brought a swift break in diplomatic ties between Baghdad and Beirut which ordered the shutdown of the Iraqi embassy.
Lebanese authorities said in 1995 they were waiting for a reply by Lebanon's foreign ministry to whether the suspects were listed as diplomats or non-diplomatic staff.
The judicial sources said the ministry confirmed the suspects' diplomatic identity last week. They gave no explanation for the prolonged delay in the ministry's response.
The sources said that Suheil's family could appeal against the decision to bail them out to a committee comprising three judges.
A fourth diplomat, commercial attache Khaled Khalaf who was also arrested in connection with the murder, had died in custody of a brain haemorrhage in June 1995. He had not faced trial.
